population.note: FICTIONAL. Of ~275M adults: 28.4% current ≈ 78.1M; 40.0% ever ≈ 110M; used-and-off-now 11.6% ≈ 31.9M; never-used 60% ≈ 165M. Cycling arithmetic: ever 40.0 − current 28.4 = 11.6 pts off now; ≈14.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course and ≈5.2 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (14.0+5.2)/40.0 = 48% cycled. This is consistent with the parent's ~35% one-year persistence (~45–50% under gated plans) and 36–47% restart within a year. Ever-use rose 4.5 pts (inside the 6.4 limit) and current use rose 3.4. Most of the 2032–34 growth came from three groups: ≈4.8M lean 'metabolic baseline' subscribers, ≈1.6M uninsured adults in the free community programme, and ≈3.6M additional Medicare users as more people aged into the benefit. Age check: 18–29 16% × 52M = 8.3M; 30–49 31.2% × 91M = 28.4M; 50–64 42% × 62M = 26.0M; 65+ 22% × 70M = 15.4M; total 78.1M = 28.4%. The rise in the 18–29 and 30–49 bands is mostly the longevity/'baseline' and 'focus' trade among top-third professionals with BMI under 27. The 65+ rise came from aging-in and from DEXA capacity catching up. Roughly one in six 65+ ever-users is on a medically advised pause, down from one in five. Income thirds average ≈28.3%. The bottom third rose from 21% to 25% through the community programme and four more continuation-standard Medicaid states. About 3.0M imported/counterfeit users remain, under-measured. Never-users (~165M) are increasingly under-30, rural, people with contraindications, and a growing self-identified 'unmedicated' minority that is now organised rather than merely absent. Pediatric: 0.75% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 550k. That figure peaked at ≈0.9% (≈650k) in mid-2033 and fell after the September 2033 FDA growth communication, as parents stopped or paused adolescents who had started at 12–14 and under-12 off-label use largely ended. About two children in five now live with at least one parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Part D obesity benefit (permanent since Jan 2032): eligibility BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with one comorbidity. The negotiated rate fell from $199 to $169 on 1 Jan 2034 under the Nov 2033 HHS 'bridge' agreement. The $50 copay and the counselling visit are unchanged. Retatrutide 12 mg was added in Jul 2033 with a step requirement (failing to reach <5% loss on semaglutide or tirzepatide). Medicare pays 20.7% of fills ≈ 16.2M users (≈14.9M aged 65+ plus ≈1.3M disabled under-65): ≈6.6M diabetes and ≈9.6M obesity. 2034 obesity-benefit spend: 9.6M × $169 × 12 ≈ $19.5B gross; beneficiaries pay 9.6M × $50 × 12 ≈ $5.8B; net to the programme ≈ $13.7B, roughly flat against 2032 because the price fell as volume rose. All Medicare incretin fills: 16.2M × $169 × 12 ≈ $32.9B gross. Medicaid: 35 states plus DC have now adopted the continuation standard for the 90% match. Medicaid pays 14.6% of fills ≈ 11.4M × $169 × 12 ≈ $23.1B gross before supplemental rebates. New free provision: the Community Metabolic Access Program (CMAP, FY2034 appropriations, Dec 2033) appropriates $3.2B/yr through HRSA. It supplies oral semaglutide or Foundayo free at the point of care through federally qualified health centres to uninsured adults under 200% FPL with BMI ≥30, prioritising the 15 non-adopting states. At the $149 programme price, 1.6M enrollees × $149 × 12 ≈ $2.9B/yr, inside the appropriation. CMAP enrollees are subject to the continuation-standard weigh-ins.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $4–25/month, with generic oral semaglutide and liraglutide–semaglutide combinations exported widely. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies at scale, and Chinese API still underlies most of the gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 45–70/month. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey, Egypt, and now the UK and EU (semaglutide exclusivity lapsed 2031–33) have generics. US: the 2031 settlements set entry for 2033, but FDA issued complete response letters to the lead ANDA filers in Mar 2033, citing peptide-impurity and immunogenicity characterisation and API from a Chinese site under import alert. No US generic launched in 2033 or 2034, and resubmissions are pending with decisions expected 2035.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline. The Nov 2033 HHS–manufacturer 'bridge-to-generic' agreement, signed after the generic delay, sets these prices from Jan 2034: Medicare/Medicaid $199→$169; federal direct portal (launched as TrumpRx) injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $199–279→$169–229; retatrutide 12 mg direct $399→$329 (list unchanged at $1,499); amycretin direct $449→$379; MariTide (approved Aug 2033) $349 direct; survodutide $299 direct. Oral starting doses hold at $149–150. Brands hold the $150–300 band and coverage still rations access. PBM net ≈ $150–170 under outcomes contracts. Payer mix of ≈78.1M users: commercial 41.1% (32.1M), Medicare 20.7% (16.2M), Medicaid 14.6% (11.4M), CMAP free provision 2.0% (1.6M), cash/direct 17.7% (13.8M, of which ≈4.2M 'calm/focus' and ≈4.8M 'metabolic baseline' subscribers with BMI <27, plus ≈4.8M cash obesity users), imported/counterfeit 3.8% (3.0M); sum 78.1M. Imports fell for the first time in absolute terms as CMAP and portal cuts reached the uninsured. ≈80% of covering employers use outcome-gated designs, and ≈40% of large employers now run 'treat-or-pay' wellness surcharges under the 2033 tri-agency rule. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose, allocation lifted May 2033)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Feb 2033)
GIP-receptor antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide, approved Aug 2033 with DEXA monitoring)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: adolescent obesity 12+ (semaglutide, liraglutide; label revised Sep 2033 to require growth-velocity and pubertal-stage monitoring)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic baseline' / longevity low-dose plans for adults with BMI <27 (≈4.8M subscribers; concierge chains, telehealth and pharmacy clinics; lifestyle-account reimbursable at many large employers)
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS-endpoint trial still enrolling)
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care (sharply curtailed after Sep 2033)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple_agonist_30pct driver is again met by an existing product in a new form and a wider launch. Retatrutide 12 mg (30.1% at 104 weeks, approved Feb 2031) came off allocation in May 2033, when Lilly's expanded North Carolina fill-finish lines came online. It was added to Part D with a step requirement in Jul 2033, and by end-2034 ≈4.5M Americans use it. Both products under review at the start were approved: survodutide (Feb 2033, chronic weight management, DEXA in label, modest uptake) and MariTide (Aug 2033, monthly dosing, approved after 72-week DEXA data, lean-mass statement in label). Neither added an indication. Bimagrumab + semaglutide filed in Apr 2034 (phase 3 complete). It cannot be approved before Apr 2035 and is the most watched decision of 2035. The smoking-cessation trial is still enrolling. The longevity_wellness driver is realised off-label: no sponsor has filed a 'metabolic health' indication in normal-weight adults, and FDA has said in public meetings that one would need hard outcomes. Incretin market ≈$180B in 2034: US ≈$155B (≈75.1M paying users × ≈$172 average net × 12), ex-US ≈$25B and eroding further with European generics.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. More frequent during 12 mg retatrutide escalation, which is now widespread off allocation. Low in baseline-dose lean users.
Rising in absolute numbers with retatrutide's wider use and the 15.4M-strong 65+ population.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Counterfeit cases still confound reporting, though less as imports decline.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL bellwether trials scheduled for 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A 2034 Medicare claims update estimates ≈1.7M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria, up from ≈1.3M. In untrained users over 50, lean mass is ~30–40% of weight lost. In lean 'baseline' users the absolute loss is small but unstudied.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label retained. Body-composition monitoring is now in the retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin, survodutide and MariTide labels. The CMS annual DEXA requirement continues. MA strength benefits keep expanding.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.0M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. At a ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess, that is ≈16,800 excess hip fractures a year against ~300,000 US total, plus a vertebral tail among cycling postmenopausal women. Medicare DEXA claims are up ~170% since 2028. Waits have eased to 6–12 weeks in most regions as mobile and pharmacy-clinic DEXA spread, but are still longer in the rural South.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained. Bone endpoints are required in all filings. The CMS 90-day bone-pause code continues. Private gated plans are still not bound by it, apart from union contracts that copy it. The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in adults. The adolescent psychiatric review (2033–34) examined it again and still found no association.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Retatrutide SHAPS postmarketing: ~12% of 12 mg users versus ~5% of comparators; observational and dose-dependent. With ≈4.5M on retatrutide 12 mg and ≈3M on other top-dose regimens, that implies roughly 500–600k excess cases of clinically meaningful anhedonia if causal. The ≈9.0M low-dose 'calm/focus' and 'baseline' subscribers remain unmeasured except in vendor surveys.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FTC consent orders still bar 'anxiety treatment' claims. 'Calm', 'focus' and now 'metabolic youth' wording is permitted. No label change; an FDA advisory committee on the class is scheduled for 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Millions of regain episodes a year from gating, continuation-standard suspensions, bone pauses and adolescent stops after the growth communication.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The CMS bone-pause code applies to Medicare. The Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver in Feb 2034 (2–1); cert petition pending.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency are common in high-loss older users and in adolescents with rapid loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Part D and CMAP counselling templates include a protein and vitamin D screen. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use. Adolescent findings are now tracked as a separate entry.
Poison-centre calls down slightly for the first time since 2029, as imported/counterfeit users fell from ≈3.8M to ≈3.0M. Steady dosing-error and infection cases continue.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and seizures continue. The 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled. Individuals are still not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. Absolute numbers are rising with the population, and rates are slightly lower where MA strength benefits are used.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening is mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging. DEXA cohorts with three or more cycles replicate the finding: same weight, less lean mass and more visceral fat, worst in people over 50.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 2034 joint society guidance advises against elective cycling. No regulatory action, and gated plans still cause involuntary cycling.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A rise of several bpm in mean resting heart rate at 12 mg. A 2034 interim CVOT look showed no MACE excess, and arrhythmia significance remains unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled as a precaution; CVOT continues to 2036.

safety_ledger.effect: Pediatric growth and pubertal development (adolescents who started at 12–14)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Pooled postmarketing registries and Medicaid EPSDT claims (Sep 2033) show height-velocity deceleration of ~1–1.5 cm/yr against expected, and delayed Tanner progression, in a subset of adolescents who started at 12–14 and lost more than 15% of body weight. The subset is concentrated in early-pubertal boys. It coheres with the 2032 bone-accrual readout. Final adult height is unknown because the oldest exposed cohort is only now finishing growth. The absolute numbers are small but involve tens of thousands of exposed children.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Sep 2033). Adolescent labels now require baseline and 6-monthly height velocity and Tanner staging. AAP guidance advises against starting before Tanner 4 except in severe obesity. FDA moved the full adolescent data deadline up to 2034, and sponsors submitted interim data in Oct 2034.

safety_ledger.effect: Restrictive eating and eating-disorder presentations in adolescents
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Adolescent eating-disorder clinics report more ARFID-like and restrictive presentations among teens who stopped the drug and feared regain, and among non-users whose households are on it. Confounding by household culture is severe, and no causal analysis exists.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Included in the AAP guidance update; no FDA action.

food_and_beverage.state: With 28% of adults on the drug and ~9M lean subscribers eating less too, US salty-snack volume falls ~4% a year and confectionery ~5%. A third large packaged-food group sold its candy portfolio to private equity in 2033. 'Bone-forward' fortified dairy, protein and 'baseline' functional lines lead growth. An opposite niche has appeared: 'unmedicated' heritage baking, whole-milk and full-fat lines, and seasonal 'feast' SKUs, branded around appetite and growing from a small base in Atlanta, Nashville and the Ozarks.

alcohol.state: Seventh straight year of US spirits volume decline; beer also down. 'Calm' and 'baseline' subscribers rarely drink on weeknights. Non-alcoholic, 'one good drink' premium and, newly, 'unmedicated bar' nights at Nashville and Austin venues hold up. Tobacco and vape volumes keep falling faster than pre-2028 trend.

restaurants.state: Spend per cover is ~10–12% below 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced bowls and half portions are the default. 'Full table' weekend nights are now a chain format, and 'no-gram' heritage rooms in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston have become a destination category marketed to the unmedicated. Value buffets keep closing.

apparel.state: Size churn continues with gating drop-offs and pauses. Cycling-sized rental and resale keeps growing. A small 'soft tailoring' line pitched at the unmedicated aesthetic has gained shelf space at two department chains.

fitness.state: Growing. 'Prescribed lifting' is standard in MA. Pharmacy-clinic DEXA and strip-mall coaching chains roughly doubled scan capacity in two years. Longevity clinics bundle 'baseline' doses with VO2max and grip-strength testing. Qualified trainers for older lifters remain the binding constraint.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is 70%, and ~80% of it is gated. Under the 2033 tri-agency wellness rule, ≈40% of large employers now waive a BMI surcharge of up to 30% of premium for anyone with verified adherence to a prescribed regimen, which in effect means 'treat or pay'. Pharmacy trend is ~+3% as volume rises ~15% at prices down ~12%. Fracture and fall costs keep shifting to Medicare Part A and MA. Life insurers ask the 'why not treated' question as standard.

pharma.state: Volume up ~15%, average net down ~10–12%, US revenue up ~7% to ≈$155B. Lilly dominates through retatrutide 12 mg and Foundayo. Novo holds Medicare semaglutide and amycretin and gained two years from the generic delay. Amgen's MariTide takes the monthly niche. Boehringer's survodutide is small. Indian and Chinese makers win in Europe and wait on FDA resubmissions.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among insured adults over 40, being on the drug is unremarkable and being off needs a reason. Two new readings have appeared. A lean 35-year-old with trained shoulders and a 'baseline' plan signals self-management money. A visibly soft, well-fed body worn deliberately, with linen, bread and a 'Fed' pin, signals 'unmedicated' membership rather than neglect, at least in the places where the movement is strong.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use is still converging (bottom 25%, top 31%), but care quality is diverging further. The top third runs retatrutide or MariTide with DEXA, antiresorptives and lifting, and increasingly doses its lean children's parents for 'longevity'. The bottom third is on CMAP orals at an FQHC with kiosk weigh-ins, or on Medicaid continuation standards. In treat-or-pay workplaces, declining the drug costs a warehouse worker up to 30% more in premium, so the price of refusal is regressive.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first shared meals are the norm, and hosts plan for 'on' guests by default. The unmedicated movement has turned long-table feasts into deliberate public ritual: monthly 'Whole Table' suppers in Atlanta's West End, Tulsa church halls and East Nashville backyards, with bread broken by hand and seconds offered as a point of principle.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps carry on/off/pausing/'baseline' fields. 'Unmedicated' has grown from a niche filter into a sizeable sub-scene, and one app built around it, Appetite, crossed a million users in 2034. Advice columns field both complaints: a partner who refuses to start, and a partner who started 'baseline' with no weight to lose.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Medicalised and assumed to be managed for most. Opposition has consolidated into an 'unmedicated' identity movement with its own aesthetics: soft tailoring, full-fat cooking, 'written/played/raised unmedicated' marks. Its politics run across the usual lines. Atlanta body-sovereignty collectives, Tulsa–Dallas 'appetite is a gift' congregations, rural medical-freedom Republicans, disability lawyers and, since Sep 2033, parents of adolescents organised as 'Raised Whole' all oppose treat-or-pay surcharges and pediatric prescribing. It remains a minority. Polling puts self-identified 'unmedicated by conviction' adults at ~8%, concentrated among under-35s and in Georgia, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Vermont.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Top-dose regimens: ≈4.5M on retatrutide 12 mg plus ≈3M on other top doses. At the ~12% versus ~5% SHAPS rates that implies ≈500–600k excess clinically meaningful anhedonia cases if causal. Low-dose 'calm/focus' (≈4.2M) and 'metabolic baseline' (≈4.8M) subscribers, ≈9.0M people mostly without obesity, are unmeasured apart from vendor surveys, which report 'reduced reactivity' as a satisfaction metric.
interior_life.framing: Feature in retail, side effect in clinic, character to the unmedicated. 'Quiet', 'Even', 'Unhooked' and the newer 'Baseline' plans ($149–199/month) sell calm, focus and 'metabolic youth'. Prescribers say 'reward modulation'. Users call the bad version 'the grey'. The unmedicated call the whole effect 'the flattening' and treat feeling it as a moral matter.
interior_life.effect_on_work: 'Focus' and 'baseline' plans are lifestyle-account staples at large white-collar employers, and longevity clinics sell them to firms as executive benefits. Warehouses and fleets favour continuous use, and under treat-or-pay rules a worker with BMI ≥30 who declines pays more. Sales, hospitality and creative workers still dose down before peaks. Unions in Ohio and Michigan auto plants and in hospital systems bargained surcharge waivers and bone-pause clauses into 2034 contracts.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Critics' 'grey era' of mid-tempo pop has a counter-scene. 'Played unmedicated' shows in East Nashville and Atlanta sell out, and the tag is now a marketing category with its own festival (Whole Fest, Chattanooga, Sep 2034). Extreme sports, spicy food and loud venues keep growing among users chasing stimulus. Comedians on both sides mine the 'baseline bro'.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose and subscriptions. Dose-holiday weekends and 'restart' anti-nausea packs are routine. Mixed couples, one on 'Quiet' and one unmedicated by conviction, are a recognised counselling category, and parenting disputes over a teenager's prescription have reached family courts in several states.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The fight has shifted from who pays to what refusing costs. Treat-or-pay surcharges, continuation-standard weigh-ins and pediatric prescribing unite an odd coalition. Oklahoma and Vermont passed 'Appetite Freedom' laws in 2034 banning BMI-linked premium surcharges in state-regulated plans, and those laws do not reach self-insured ERISA plans. Republicans split between accountability and medical freedom. Democrats defend CMAP and the continuation standard while hedging on pediatrics. Senior groups still lobby on DEXA capacity.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and now pediatric-focused: DEXA in every filing, body-composition monitoring in four labels, a growth communication with label changes for adolescents, and CRLs to lead generic semaglutide filers on impurity and immunogenicity grounds. That last decision was defended as rigour and attacked as protectionism. Import enforcement is selective with no individual prosecutions. FTC regulates claims by consent order and has not touched 'baseline' or longevity language.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Part D obesity benefit at $169 from Jan 2034 ($50 copay). 90% Medicaid match in 35 states plus DC. Direct free provision through CMAP: $3.2B/yr, FQHC-dispensed oral semaglutide or Foundayo for uninsured adults under 200% FPL, ≈1.6M enrolled. No individual mandate, but the 2033 tri-agency wellness rule lets employers make surcharge relief contingent on verified adherence.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard (≥80% PDC, 6-monthly verified weight, ≥5% at 6 months or override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, 90-day bone pause) now also covers CMAP. Two missed verifications suspend coverage for 6 months. Indiana and Arkansas keep 12-month lockouts, which the Seventh Circuit upheld in Feb 2034. Employer gating covers ~80% of plans. Treat-or-pay surcharges rely on pharmacy-claims adherence feeds from PBMs to wellness vendors, and that data flow is the movement's central grievance.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide, and fleets require DEXA for drivers over 55. The Army now allows accession waivers after 12 months stable on therapy, matching the Air Force. Recruiters report applicants citing 'Raised Whole' parents who refused adolescent prescriptions.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product supply the world, and Europe's generics now draw on them too. FDA's CRLs named a Chinese API site under import alert, which Beijing protested and Indian filers used to argue for India-sourced API. Section 232 tariffs remain. Lilly's North Carolina expansion ended 12 mg allocation, and manufacturers cite the domestic capacity to justify holding brand prices at $150–300.

events.event: FDA issues complete response letters to the lead generic semaglutide filers, citing impurity and immunogenicity data and a Chinese API site under import alert; settled 2033 US generic entry slips to 2035 at the earliest

Lilly lifts allocation on 12 mg retatrutide as new North Carolina fill-finish lines open; Medicare adds it to the Part D obesity benefit in July behind a semaglutide/tirzepatide step, and FDA approves Amgen's monthly MariTide in August with DEXA monitoring

Labor, HHS and Treasury finalise a wellness-program rule letting employers waive BMI surcharges of up to 30% of premium for workers with pharmacy-verified adherence to a prescribed regimen; within a year about 40% of large employers adopt 'treat or pay' designs

FDA safety communication reports slowed height growth and delayed puberty in a subset of adolescents who started weight drugs at 12–14 and lost heavily, and orders growth monitoring on labels; the 'Raised Whole' parents' pledge passes a million signatures in five weeks

HHS and manufacturers sign a 'bridge-to-generic' deal cutting the Medicare and Medicaid rate from $199 to $169 and portal injectables to $169–229 from January; in December, FY2034 appropriations fund $3.2 billion a year for free oral incretins at community health centres

A national pharmacy chain opens 'Metabolic Baseline' clinics offering low-dose plans to adults with BMI under 27 at $149–199 a month, and a major HR benefits platform lists them beside 'focus' subscriptions; industry surveys count about 4.8 million lean subscribers

open_tensions: Generic semaglutide was supposed to arrive in 2033 and now waits on 2035 resubmissions. Medicare's $169 rate, CMAP's budget and every state's continuation-standard math are priced against a cliff that keeps moving, while ≈3.0M people still inject $5–25 pens from Hyderabad and Shenzhen.

Treat-or-pay makes refusal expensive for adults just as the pediatric growth signal and the unmedicated movement make refusal respectable for families. Oklahoma and Vermont ban surcharges, but their laws cannot reach the self-insured ERISA plans that cover most of the workers affected.

About 9M people without obesity take low-dose incretins for 'calm', 'focus' or 'metabolic youth'. Nobody measures their bones, their reward function or their outcomes, and FDA's 2035 advisory committee is the first forum that could.

Excess hip fractures are ≈16,800 a year and rising with Medicare enrolment. Part D shows a flat net obesity cost because price fell as volume rose, while the fractures, falls and sarcopenia rehabilitation land in Part A and Medicare Advantage, where no budget score counts them. Gated employer plans still lack the bone-pause protection Medicare gives.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The 503B compounding exclusion and the 503A injunction still stand, and no individual has been prosecuted for importing pens.

prose.headline: Treat or Pay: Your Boss Can Now Charge You for Not Taking It, Your Kid's Doctor Wants You to Stop, and the Generic Never Came
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034, a little more than one American adult in four is on an incretin drug, and four in ten have taken one at some point. Most of the growth in the past two years did not come from people with obesity. About five million lean adults now take low doses under the name 'metabolic baseline', in pharmacy clinics and longevity practices that sell it beside grip-strength tests and VO2max readouts. Another four million buy 'calm' or 'focus'. None of this is approved. The FDA has said a longevity indication would need hard outcomes, and nobody has filed for one. The subscriptions are reimbursable from many employers' lifestyle accounts all the same.

The generic that was supposed to change everything did not arrive. In March 2033 the FDA rejected the first generic semaglutide applications, citing impurity data and a Chinese ingredient plant under import alert, and the settled 2033 entry date became a 2035 hope. Prices fell anyway, slowly and by agreement. In November the government and the manufacturers signed what officials called a bridge deal. Medicare's rate dropped from $199 to $169, and injectable pens on the federal portal now cost $169 to $229. The cheapest pills are still $149. Brand prices are lower but still brand prices, and coverage, with its conditions, is still what decides who gets the drug.

The conditions have spread. A 2033 federal wellness rule lets employers waive a premium surcharge of up to thirty percent for workers whose pharmacy records show they take a prescribed regimen. About four in ten large employers now use it. The benefits trade calls it 'adherence-based relief'. Warehouse workers call it treat or pay. Medicare and the thirty-five Medicaid states keep their weigh-in kiosks and bone scans. A new federal programme gives oral pills free to uninsured low-income adults through community health centres, under the same weigh-in rules. It is the first time the drug has been free for anyone, and 1.6 million people have enrolled.

The strongest pen is now easy to get. Lilly ended rationing of its thirty-percent triple agonist in May 2033, Medicare added it behind a step requirement, and four and a half million people use it. Amgen's monthly injection was approved that summer. Every new label requires body scans. The older users who make up Medicare's largest-ever drug purchase account for an estimated seventeen thousand excess hip fractures a year. Those fractures are billed to a different part of Medicare from the pens, so neither budget shows the full cost.

The event that changed the mood was about children. In September 2033 the FDA reported that some adolescents who had started at twelve to fourteen and lost weight fast were growing more slowly and going through puberty later than expected. The labels now require growth checks every six months. Pediatric use, which had been climbing, fell. Within five weeks a pledge called Raised Whole had a million parent signatures.

That pledge gave the older backlash a centre and a style. 'Unmedicated' is now an identity with its own clothes, suppers and festival, and a dating app with a million users. It is strongest in Atlanta's West End, Tulsa's church halls and East Nashville, and among people under thirty-five. Its politics cross the usual lines: rural medical-freedom conservatives, body-sovereignty collectives and disability lawyers. Oklahoma and Vermont have banned BMI premium surcharges, though the bans do not reach most large employers' plans.

The quiet feeling is still for sale, and one top-dose user in eight may lose some capacity for pleasure. Everyone who earns a living from the drug is waiting for 2035.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Vega clocks in at the pharmacy in Mesa at seven and wipes down the kiosk before the first weigh-in. Mr. Daley, CMAP, free pills, month six. He steps on, holds still for the camera, and the screen turns green. He says thank you as if she had done it.

At ten her own phone buzzes: her plan's adherence feed has synced and her surcharge waiver renewed. She is on tirzepatide through the school district's plan, where her husband works. The copay is forty dollars, and stopping would cost them two hundred eighty a month in premium. She has never once thought about stopping.

At lunch she eats half a chicken bowl and texts her sister Inés, who has a 'Fed' pin on her apron at the bakery in Tempe and stopped returning the pharmacy's reminder calls two years ago. Inés sends back a picture of a loaf.

Teo's appointment is at four. He is thirteen and stopped semaglutide in October, after the letter. The nurse measures him against the wall twice. Half a centimetre since July. Dr. Achebe says it's fine, it's within range, they'll check again in three months. Teo asks if he can have the vending-machine chips. Marisol says yes, because he looks at her as if he expects a no.

At dinner she makes rice with the chicken and puts the pot in the middle of the table. Teo has seconds. She watches him and doesn't say anything about it, and she doesn't feel much either.

least_plausible_claims.quote: In November the government and the manufacturers signed what officials called a bridge deal.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the generic delay removed the main pressure on brand prices, and the parent's 2032 talks collapsed over tariffs and supply allocation. The candidate gives no reason manufacturers would now cut Medicare to $169 and portal injectables to $169–229, so the price cut is asserted rather than shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Imports fell for the first time in absolute terms as CMAP and portal cuts reached the uninsured.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: imported users fall 21% (3.8M to 3.0M) in a year, but CMAP enrolls only 1.6M, and the portal cuts took effect only in Jan 2034 and still leave $169+ pens against $5–25 imports. Many CMAP users were never importers, so the attribution is thin.

Mechanism: the 2032 cash/direct group was 13.5M with 3.5M calm/focus subscribers, so about 10M cash obesity users. This falls to 4.8M in 2034 while portal prices drop, with no explanation. Cash obesity users halving looks like a convenient plug to make the 13.8M cash segment sum.

rationale.badness: Autonomy is the worst dimension: treat-or-pay surcharges of up to 30% of premium regressively price warehouse workers into the drug, and PBM adherence feeds go to wellness vendors. Harms also include about 16,800 excess hip fractures a year, an unmeasured ~9M low-dose users without obesity, and a pediatric growth and puberty signal. Offsetting these, CMAP free provision, $169 pricing and easing DEXA waits reduce some access harms. The result is a harder society with new losers, not a structural catastrophe.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All drivers are visibly realised. Adoption is +3.4pp, managed_decline is the Nov 2033 deal, treat-or-pay is the 2033 wellness rule, CMAP is the subsidy, the Sep 2033 FDA communication is the pediatric signal, 'unmedicated' is natural_movement, and retatrutide 12 mg satisfies the triple agonist as an existing product with a wider launch. Longevity is realised off-label with no filing, which fits the rules. mechanism: The price cut after the generic CRLs (claim 1), the import drop (claim 2) and the halved cash obesity group (claim 3) are asserted rather than shown. The 4.8M lean subscribers also appear very quickly after the May 2034 chain launch. Pediatric and treat-or-pay chains are well shown. magnitude: Population figures (28.4%, ever 40.0%), income thirds, the age-band sum to 78.1M, the payer-mix shares and the Medicare, Medicaid and CMAP dollar arithmetic all reconcile. Survodutide and MariTide approvals fit the rules, bimagrumab is correctly deferred, and generic_us stays false. Small gaps remain: 14.9M of the 15.4M users aged 65+ are on Medicare, and net Medicare spend is called 'roughly flat' while rising from $12.2B to $13.7B.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The 65+ rise came from aging-in and from DEXA capacity catching up.
